title: Loading / Error / Data States
prompt:
Render a fetch flow as a discriminated union so callers must handle every branch.

**Requirements:**
1. Import `useEffect` and `useState` from `react`.
2. Define and export:
   - `type Article = { id: number; title: string }`.
   - `type AsyncState<T> = { status: 'idle' } | { status: 'loading' } | { status: 'success'; data: T } | { status: 'error'; error: Error }`.
3. Export a function component `ArticleList({ url }: { url: string })`. Use `useState<AsyncState<Article[]>>({ status: 'idle' })`.
4. In `useEffect([url])`:
   - Set state to `{ status: 'loading' }`.
   - Call `fetch(url)` and parse JSON. On success, set `{ status: 'success', data }`. On failure, set `{ status: 'error', error }`.
5. Render a different sub-tree per status: `loading...`, `error: <message>`, or a `<ul>` of titles. Show nothing for `idle`.
hints: Modeling the four states as a discriminated union forces the renderer to handle each branch -- TS will complain if you skip one.
Don't keep separate `loading`, `error`, `data` booleans -- they create impossible states (loading + error?).
Always map non-Error throwables (`unknown`) to a real `Error` so consumers can read `.message` without ceremony.
